subject: Behavioral Economics
title: What Is Game Theory?
description: A quick win: understand What Is Game Theory?.

hook.text: Two suspects sit in separate rooms. Each must decide: confess or stay silent.

buildup.text: Game theory studies strategic decisions where your outcome depends on others' choices.

discovery.text: John Nash proved every game has at least one equilibrium: a point where no player benefits from changing their strategy.

twist.text: Nash equilibria are often not optimal. Both prisoners confess though both staying silent gives a better joint outcome.

climax.text: Game theory reveals a key truth: rational self-interest can produce collectively irrational outcomes.

punchline.text: Your best move depends on theirs. That is the game.

quiz.question: What did Nash prove about games?
options: The most aggressive player always wins
Every game has at least one equilibrium point
Cooperation is always the optimal strategy

details.summary: Game theory is the mathematical study of strategic interaction where each player's outcome depends on the choices of all players. It provides frameworks like Nash equilibrium for predicting behavior in competitive and cooperative situations.
details.whyItMatters: Game theory underpins economics, political science, evolutionary biology, and AI. It explains why nations arm, firms price competitively, and people cooperate, providing the foundation for behavioral game theory's empirical insights.
takeaways: Strategic interaction means your best choice depends on others' choices
Nash equilibrium is the central solution concept in classical game theory
Behavioral game theory studies how real humans deviate from predictions

faq.question: What is Nash equilibrium in simple terms?
faq.answer: A Nash equilibrium is a set of strategies where no player can improve their outcome by changing their strategy alone. Everyone is doing their best given what everyone else is doing. It is a stable state where no one wants to deviate.

faq.question: Why is game theory important for behavioral economics?
faq.answer: Game theory provides the rational benchmark against which behavioral deviations are measured. Without knowing what perfectly rational players would do, we cannot identify or quantify the biases and social preferences that real humans exhibit.
